item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E004","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"IMCO reported that corruption risks in federal public procurement increased from 2021 to 2022 in 184 of 260 institutions, while the federal institutions’ highest-risk axis was competition, scoring 70/100; 38% of procurement spending was directly awarded, 25% of tenders had three or fewer participants, and substantial contracting information was missing or published late.","notes":["The excerpt supports 70/100 for the federal institutions’ competition axis, not explicitly a single aggregate federal competition-risk score."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E005","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"IMCO reported that federal institutions awarded contracts to suppliers sanctioned by the public-service authority, that 74% of medicine spending was directly awarded, and that Diconsa directly awarded 90% of its 19.734 billion pesos in procurement; it recommended strengthening competition, supplier information, and oversight.","notes":["The supplied excerpt supports contracts with sanctioned suppliers but does not mention shell companies."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"RSF reported that President López Obrador and other state figures used violent and stigmatizing rhetoric against journalists, including a weekly government segment in which the press was sought to be discredited; it also reported that threats and attacks, rather than formal censorship laws, constrained journalism, while López Obrador had not undertaken needed reforms against violence and impunity.","notes":["The excerpt specifically attributes the lack of needed reforms to López Obrador, not to authorities generally."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E009","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"APECIC exempted participating companies from specified import procedures and permits, suspended review of regulations considered likely to increase food-import or domestic transport costs, maintained fuel and electricity price-containment policy, froze specified highway rates through February 28, 2023, and authorized consumer-protection verification and sanctions for detected abuses.","notes":["The excerpt says fuel and electricity price increases were contained under an existing policy; it expressly freezes highway rates, not fuel or electricity rates."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E010","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":["The excerpt is an explicitly argumentative opinion article; the claims are presented as the author's account."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E011","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E012","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0045-E013","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
